_schema: Each claim has a status and checks. A check names a ledger entry id and the law, mechanism, metric and value it must have (or an exact field for measurement entries). tests/test_foundation.py verifies every check against results/evidence_ledger.jsonl. 'unverified' claims carry no checks and must not be used as findings.

claims.statement: On needs_expansion, M1 and M2 never recover the law (0/30 runs).
claims.caveat: Expected by construction: tanh is not in the base space H0 (control test in tests/test_core.py).

claims.statement: On needs_expansion, M3 expands the library in 30/30 runs and selects the exact true terms in 30/30 runs.
claims.caveat: The expansion library EXPANSION_LIB was written to contain the true operator. This shows the mechanism works when the operator is pre-specified. It does not show open-ended discovery.

claims.statement: On in_space, the recovered-count difference between M2 and M1 is 2 of 30 runs (below the pre-registered MCID of 0.2, i.e. 6 runs).
claims.caveat: Single 30-seed comparison. Not a power calculation. Says only that the observed difference is below the pre-registered MCID.

claims.statement: On the null law, false terms are selected in at most 5% of runs for each mechanism.
claims.caveat: Counts are out of 30 runs per mechanism (57-63%). BIC selection over subsets does not control false discoveries at n=30.

claims.statement: The exp01 runs.csv is reproduced byte-for-byte by the current code, and the ledger's measurement entries cite that file's SHA-256.
claims.caveat: Verified by tests/test_foundation.py::test_reproduces_committed_exp01 and by hashing the file on disk.

claims.statement: LLM agents can (or cannot) discover laws better than the algorithmic mechanisms at equal budget.
claims.caveat: No LLM was queried. Requires API approval. Not a finding.

claims.statement: External benchmarks report that most AI-agent research outputs fail provenance checks (figures from the strategy document).
claims.caveat: Primary sources not opened (see docs/ROADMAP.md, section 'to verify'). Must not be cited as fact.

claims.statement: Plain BIC selection (M2) does not control false discoveries on the null law: null false-term rate on test seeds is above 5%.
claims.caveat: Test seeds 0-199, one law, sigma 0.1, budget 30.

claims.statement: The calibrated margin rule (margin 10, the grid edge) brings the null false-term rate under 5% on test seeds, while in_space exact recovery stays at 1.00.
claims.caveat: Margin 10 is the largest grid value; the true threshold may be higher. Not tested beyond the grid.

claims.statement: Exact recovery on in_space is at ceiling for both M1 and M2, so the active-vs-fixed comparison cannot be tested with exact_terms.
claims.caveat: A zero mean difference at ceiling is not evidence that active design has no effect.

claims.statement: Doubling the budget reduces median RMSE of M1 on in_space by about 28% (ratio 0.721), so the RMSE endpoint can see effects of this size.
On in_space, the median RMSE ratio M2/M1 is 0.767 with 95% CI [0.698, 0.843], which meets the frozen supported rule.
claims.caveat: The same metric gives ratio 0.917 on the null law (C-13). The in_space result does NOT show that active design finds laws better.

claims.statement: On the null law the RMSE ratio M2/M1 is 0.917 (CI reaches 1.00): the RMSE endpoint rewards M2 even when there is no law.
claims.caveat: Finite-sample effect; motivates the measured null baseline (C-14).

claims.statement: The measured null median RMSE of M1 (0.0416) differs by more than 20% from the P26 formula 1.63*sigma/sqrt(N) (0.0298), so the formula is not used as the baseline.
claims.caveat: Measured on calibration seeds 1000-1199 only. The formula matches M2 and M3 medians closely, so it is not wrong for them, only not general.

claims.statement: Without expansion (A1 and A2) the agent abstains on every delay world (abstain rate 1.0 on test seeds 0-9).
claims.caveat: Holds by construction: the base space (memoryless f(x)) cannot represent a delay. It shows the abstention rule works, not that the agent discovers anything.

claims.statement: With expansion (A3) the agent names the true delay on 92.5% of delay runs (test seeds 0-9), with median holdout RMSE about 0.0024.
claims.caveat: The delay family (tau in {0.4, 0.6, 0.8, 1.0}) contains every true tau by construction, like tanh in exp01. This is search inside a pre-specified family, not discovery of a missing representation. 10 seeds, 8 worlds: descriptive.

claims.statement: A3 names no false delay on the control worlds (memoryless, weak, zero): false-delay rate 0.0.
claims.caveat: The weak world (b = 0.02) is classified as memoryless or NON_IDENTIFIABLE, which is the intended outcome, not a failure to find a delay.

claims.statement: On fresh seeds 10-19, never used in development, A3 names the true delay on 96.3% of delay runs, and the same verdicts hold.
claims.caveat: Same caveat as C-16: the delay family contains the true tau by construction. Confirmation only shows the rule is stable across seeds, not that a missing representation was found.

claims.statement: On the out-of-library law (primitive exp), M1 with the frozen exp02 threshold abstains on 100% of seeds 0-29, and the M3 expansion never names the true term. M3 still names some model on every seed.
claims.caveat: The abstention rule detects insufficiency on the base path, but the M3 expansion does not abstain: it names a wrong model every time. A constructive expansion is not claimed. Seeds 0-29, descriptive.
